sections.h2: What makes a Michigan quitclaim deed valid?
sections.html:
A deed worded in substance as "A.B. quit claims to C.D.", with the premises described and the consideration stated, is a good and sufficient quitclaim conveyance once the grantor signs, seals and acknowledges it. That rule is in MCL 565.152, part of a statute dating to 1881.

The statutory wording is short on purpose. A quitclaim passes whatever interest the grantor holds and says nothing more, so it fits a transfer between people who already know the title, such as a spouse, a parent, or a co-owner buying out a sibling.

A signed deed is only the start. The deed still has to meet the recording rules, and the transfer may bring a tax filing, a transfer tax question and a change in the property tax bill.

sections.h2: What must the deed look like before the register of deeds accepts it?
sections.html:
The register of deeds cannot take a deed for recording unless it satisfies MCL 565.201. Instruments executed after April 1, 1997 face the most detailed checklist:

  • Each signer's name printed, typed or stamped beneath the signature, in black or dark blue ink, with no mismatch against the acknowledgment.
  • The grantee's address on the deed, with a street number where street numbers are in common use.
  • The name and business address of the person who drafted it.
  • A single statement on the first line of print that identifies the recordable event.
  • A 2-1/2 inch blank margin at the top of page one and 1/2 inch on the other sides.
  • 10-point type or larger, black ink, white paper of at least 20-pound weight, between 8-1/2 by 11 and 8-1/2 by 14 inches.
  • The first five digits of any Social Security number obscured or removed.
  • An English translation attached if any part is in another language.

A notary's printed name must appear on the same page near the notary's signature. Check the checklist against your draft before driving to the county seat, because a rejected deed means a second trip.

sections.h2: Does a quitclaim deed carry Michigan transfer tax?
sections.html:
Often it does, because the tax applies to deeds given for consideration. The seller or grantor owes it, and it is paid to the county treasurer where the property sits within 15 days after the deed is delivered, according to MCL 207.523.

Two layers apply. The state tax is $3.75 for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 under MCL 207.525. The county tax is 55 cents for each $500 in a county with fewer than 2,000,000 people, and a larger county may set up to 75 cents. The deed must state the total value on its face, or an affidavit of value must be attached. When real and personal property are sold together, the tax applies only to the real property if the values are shown separately.

Ask the county treasurer or the register of deeds which affidavit form to attach, and which of the two offices collects the tax at the counter in your county.

sections.h2: Which quitclaim deeds are exempt from transfer tax?
sections.html:
The state act lists the exemptions in MCL 207.526, and the county act in MCL 207.505 has a shorter list. The ones that matter for quitclaim deeds are below.

Common transfer tax exemptions for deeds in Michigan
SituationExempt?Source
Deed to confirm title already vested, including one that corrects a flaw in titleYesMCL 207.526(n); 207.505(l)
Deed from an individual to a child, stepchild or adopted childYes (state tax)MCL 207.526(j)
Deed from an individual to a grandchild, step-grandchild or adopted grandchildYes (state tax)MCL 207.526(k)
Deed that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties between spousesYesMCL 207.526(i); 207.505(i)
Deed that creates a joint tenancy when one person already owns the propertyYesMCL 207.526(r); 207.505(o)
Consideration under $100YesMCL 207.526(a); 207.505(a)

If the tax was paid and the transfer later turns out to have qualified, the seller, or a buyer who paid on the seller's behalf, may ask Treasury for a refund in the form and manner it sets. The statute reaches back four years for transfers that qualify.

sections.h2: How is a quitclaim deed recorded, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Take the deed to the register of deeds in the county where the land lies. Under MCL 600.2567 the fee is $30 for entering and recording a document, no matter how many pages. Certified copies cost $5 each for certification, and plain copies are $1.00 per page. A charter county may set its own schedule, so confirm the figure with the office.

Where the register accepts electronic recording under the Uniform Real Property Electronic Recording Act, the fee is due within one business day of receipt rather than when the document is dropped off.

Recording protects the new owner. A conveyance that is not recorded is void against a later good-faith purchaser for value whose own deed is recorded first, and the fact that the first recorded deed is a quitclaim does not by itself put that purchaser on notice of the earlier one (MCL 565.29).

sections.h2: How does a quitclaim deed affect the property tax bill?
sections.html:
A deed is a transfer of ownership under MCL 211.27a, and the buyer or grantee must notify the city or township assessor within 45 days. Taxable value normally resets to state equalized value for the year after a transfer.

Transfers of residential property to the transferor's or spouse's parent, child, sibling or grandchild are excluded from the definition, provided the home is not put to commercial use afterward. A transfer between spouses is excluded too. Even so, the filing is worth confirming with the assessor, because a missing filing on a taxable transfer carries a $5 daily penalty with a $200 cap for a principal residence, plus back taxes. Our page on the Michigan Property Transfer Affidavit walks through the deadline and penalties.

sections.h2: When is a quitclaim deed the wrong tool for selling a house?
sections.html:
When a buyer is paying market price, they will usually want title insurance, and insurers look closely at a chain of title that includes a quitclaim. A quitclaim moves the grantor's interest without describing what that interest is, so it cannot fix a lien, a missed heir or an unpaid tax.

It also does not release a mortgage. A lender's recorded lien stays on the property after a transfer, and the new owner takes the house subject to it. Before you sign, order a title search or ask the register of deeds what is recorded against the parcel, and have a Michigan attorney review any transfer that involves a loan, a divorce, an estate or more than one co-owner.

faqs.q: Where do I record a Michigan quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: With the register of deeds in the county where the property is located. The recording fee is $30 per document under MCL 600.2567, unless a charter county has set a different schedule.

faqs.q: Is a quitclaim deed to my child exempt from transfer tax?
faqs.a: The state transfer tax exempts a conveyance from an individual to that individual's child, stepchild or adopted child (MCL 207.526(j)). Grandchildren are covered by subsection (k). Ask the county treasurer how the county tax exemption is claimed.

faqs.q: Does a quitclaim deed remove a name from the mortgage?
faqs.a: No. The deed changes who holds title and has no effect on the loan contract. The lender's lien stays recorded against the property until the loan is paid or released.

faqs.q: How soon must the transfer tax be paid?
faqs.a: Within 15 days after the deed is delivered, paid to the county treasurer where the land lies. The seller or grantor is the person liable for it.

faqs.q: Does the new owner have to tell the assessor?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. The grantee must notify the local assessing office within 45 days of a transfer of ownership, and excluded transfers such as those between spouses still deserve a call to the assessor.
